subject: POC success criteria, integration routes & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stone <alex@edgefin.com>, Priya Rao <priya@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria, integration routes & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track scope and owners. I attached a short one-pager (edgefin_poc_scope.pdf).

Goal (what success looks like):
- Validate Redwood inference for customer-facing summarization and real-time reranking in your search flow.
- Business metric: 15% lift in retrieval precision on test prompts or equivalent product KPIs in pilot cohort.

Technical success criteria (for the POC run):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) in the staging region; p95 for streaming partial token arrival consistent within 50ms of non-stream baseline.
- Throughput: sustain ~400-600 concurrent QPS on the routed model for peak test windows.
- Quality: top-3 rerank relevance >= 0.85 against your labeled test set (we'll exchange evaluation prompts).
- Stability: zero data leakage; logs and request traces must be accessible to EdgeFin SREs for the duration of the trial.

POC timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): alignment and infra prep (exchange test dataset, security contacts, IP allowlists).
- Week 1: SDK integration and model handshake; smoke tests on staging (non-prod).
- Week 2: Load tests, streaming validation, and evaluation run against labeled set.
- Week 3: Sign-off period + handover to CS if acceptance gates met.

Integration plan (high level):
- SDK: integrate our JavaScript/Go SDK to start; we recommend the streaming SDK for in-product latency-sensitive flows. We'll provide code snippets and a small sample app.
- API routes: primary routes we'll use are /v1/generate (supports streaming=true), /v1/embeddings for candidate encoding (for rerank), and /v1/agent/call for tool-calling workflows (optional; useful if you want to orchestrate search-then-generate).
- Streaming: start with streaming enabled for the UI path to validate partial responses and reduce perceived latency. We will measure p50/p95 token arrival.
- Tool calling: if you want structured tool responses (e.g., call your internal enrichment service), we can set up a secure webhook endpoint. We'll run tool calls through a sandboxed agent in staging before production.

Security / ops checklist (high level):
- We will need an IP allowlist and a service account for agent access.
- KMS usage for any customer-provided keys (if you want to keep KV cache encrypted at rest) — confirm whether EdgeFin will provide keys or we should use Redwood-managed keys for the trial.

Immediate asks / owners:
- Alex / Priya: share a representative labeled prompt set and a contact for network allowlist (owner: Alex) — due EOD Wed.
- Marissa (CS): prepare staging cluster and test credentials (owner: Marissa) — due Fri.
- Karthik (APIs): will own SDK snippets and route config (owner: Karthik) — will push initial branch by Thu.

Next steps:
1) Alex to confirm dataset + security contact.
2) We (Redwood) send API contract + sample SDK repo (I attached the scope doc).
3) Kickoff integration session (30–45m) on Thurs or Fri; suggest Thu 10:00am PT.

Attachments: edgefin_poc_scope.pdf (one-pager)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- For throughput, our initial ask is to validate 400 QPS sustained with spikes to 700 QPS for 30s bursts. Can Redwood run an autoscale policy in staging to demonstrate this?
- On quantization/accuracy tradeoffs: do you recommend an FP16 path for our first run or a quantized int8 variant? We care about inference cost but can't accept a >5% drop in relevance.
- I've added a short list of questions in question_list.xlsx (attached) — Priya will take point on engineering coordination.

Priya — I'll let you respond on allowlists and whether we need a temporary DMZ for webhooks.

—Alex
CTO, EdgeFin

Alex — thanks, good questions. Short answers below and a draft API contract attached (api_contract_draft.docx).

1) Autoscale in staging: yes — Marissa will provision a routed staging pool with autoscale capped at the agreed burst size. We will run an ingest/replay to simulate your spike pattern; Karthik will coordinate the load test script.

2) Quantization recommendation: start on FP16 for the initial quality run. If cost looks prohibitive after evaluation we can try an int8 quantized variant but only after re-evaluating the labeled set for any >5% quality drop. We will run a short A/B on the evaluation set to quantify any degradation.

3) Concrete success gates (scoped for the POC run):
- p95 token generation latency <= 220ms (we'll be conservative for streaming overhead)
- Burst handling up to 700 QPS sustained for 30s with <1% error rate
- Relevance (top3) >= 0.85 on your labeled test set (we'll exchange the csv)
- End-to-end tool call flow completes with secure webhook handshake and no elevation-of-privilege issues reported by EdgeFin SREs.

4) API routes / integration notes: 
- /v1/generate: use streaming=true for UI; fallback non-streaming for batch scoring. Include a client-side keepalive for long user sessions.
- /v1/embeddings: we recommend batching candidate encoding in 64–128 item batches to balance throughput and latency.
- /v1/agent/call: tool-calling will be proxied through a staging webhook. We will sign outbound requests with a short-lived HMAC token; EdgeFin should implement a verification middleware.

5) Data/keys: if you prefer Redwood-managed keys for the trial we can enable that immediately; if you want to bring-your-own KMS we need the onboarding steps by Thu so Legal/Compliance can sign the minimal agreement.

Attachment: api_contract_draft.docx — includes rate limits, sample cURL, and expected response shapes.

I'll schedule the Thu 10:00am PT integration session unless you prefer Fri.

Ben
